newsitem.title: USA: Canada won't accept new limits on wheat - official.
newsitem.headline: Canada won't accept new limits on wheat - official.

text.p: A Canadian government official said Tuesday that Canada would not accept any new limits on wheat shipments to the United States but would discuss differences concerning statistics on wheat trade.

The official told reporters following a White House meeting between Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and President Clinton that Canada "will not accept to renegotiate the levels" of wheat sold in the U.S. market.

But the official, who asked not to be identified, said that the Canadian government was happy to "open its books" to address U.S. concerns that some of the statistical informaiton on Canadian wheat supplies might be inaccurate.
Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton met with U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Tuesday to discuss wheat and other trade issues between the two countries.
Barshefsky heard complaints last week from North Dakota farmers who fear a flood of Canadian wheat into their markets.

"Our position is we are open and fair traders," Eggleton said at a news conference. He said Canada was meeting all its obligations under the World Trade Organization and the North American Free Trade Agreement.
"We don't see any difficulties," he said, adding that some discussions would be held later this month on the issue.
